37967-more-portmanteau-plays.title: More Portmanteau Plays
37967-more-portmanteau-plays.creator: Stuart Walker
37967-more-portmanteau-plays.description: A book by Stuart Walker. agnificent cities, and all about you laying out magnificent gardens, and, with an April pool you had made infinite seas where pirates fought or mermaids played in coral caves. Then came the Doubters, laughing and jeering at you, and you let your cities, and gardens, and seas go floating in the air--unseen, unsung--wonderful cities, and gardens, and seas, peopled with the realest of people....

43584-the-mystery-of-the-secret-band.title: The Mystery Of The Secret Band
43584-the-mystery-of-the-secret-band.creator: Edith Lavell
43584-the-mystery-of-the-secret-band.description: A book by Edith Lavell. "Oh, I wasn't so hot," laughed Mary Louise modestly. "I'll tell you who was the star of the afternoon--little Rosemary Dotts. She forgot all of her piece except the second line--'I'm going to have plum pudding!' Well, she said that once, and then she stared around at the audience and repeated it.

arxiv-2101-02962.title: Evaluating EYM amplitudes in four dimensions by refined graphic expansion
arxiv-2101-02962.creator: Hongxiang Tian, Enze Gong, Chongsi Xie, Yi-Jian Du
arxiv-2101-02962.description: Abstract The recursive expansion of tree level multitrace Einstein-Yang-Mills (EYM) amplitudes induces a refined graphic expansion, by which any tree-level EYM amplitude can be expressed as a summation over all possible refined graphs. Each graph contributes a unique coefficient as well as a proper combination of color-ordered Yang-Mills (YM) amplitudes.

arxiv-2204-11483.title: Estimation of Strong Structural Controllable Subspace of Network: Equitable Partition Method
arxiv-2204-11483.creator: Lanhao Zhao
arxiv-2204-11483.description: Abstract In this paper, the strong structural controllability of the network is analyzed. Based on the unified definition of equitable partition for kinds of scene, the upper bound of the strong structural controllable subspace in different scenarios is given, and the strong structural observability is analyzed by using the characteristics of the dual system.

arxiv-2206-11148.title: Probing the multiwavelength emission scenario of GRB 190114C
arxiv-2206-11148.creator: Marc Klinger, Donggeun Tak, Andrew M. Taylor, Sylvia J. Zhu
arxiv-2206-11148.description: Abstract Multiwavelength observation of the gamma-ray burst, GRB 190114C, opens a new window for studying the emission mechanism of GRB afterglows. Its Very-High-Energy (VHE; ≳ 100 \gtrsim 100 GeV) detection has motivated an inverse Compton interpretation for the emission, but this has not been tested.

arxiv-2301-04584.title: Continual HyperTransformer: A Meta-Learner for Continual Few-Shot Learning
arxiv-2301-04584.creator: Max Vladymyrov mxv@google.com, Andrey Zhmoginov azhmogin@google.com, Mark Sandler sandler@google.com
arxiv-2301-04584.description: Abstract We focus on the problem of learning without forgetting from multiple tasks arriving sequentially, where each task is defined using a few-shot episode of novel or already seen classes. We approach this problem using the recently published HyperTransformer (HT), a Transformer-based hypernetwork that generates specialized task-specific CNN weights directly from the support set.

arxiv-2304-00996.title: Deep Learning-based Diffusion Tensor Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Reconstruction: A Comparison Study
arxiv-2304-00996.creator: Jiahao Huang, Pedro F. Ferreira, Lichao Wang, Yinzhe Wu, Angelica I. Aviles-Rivero, Carola-Bibiane Schönlieb, Andrew D. Scott, Zohya Khalique, Maria Dwornik, Ramyah Rajakulasingam, Ranil De Silva, Dudley J. Pennell, Sonia Nielles-Vallespin, Guang Yang
arxiv-2304-00996.description: Abstract In vivo cardiac diffusion tensor imaging (cDTI) is a promising Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) technique for evaluating the micro-structure of myocardial tissue in the living heart, providing insights into cardiac function and enabling the development of innovative therapeutic strategies.

arxiv-2404-01031.title: An 𝒪 \mathcal{O} -monoidal Grothendieck construction
arxiv-2404-01031.creator: Redi Haderi and Walker H. Stern
arxiv-2404-01031.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Redi Haderi and Walker H. Stern. Given an operad 𝒪 {\mathcal{O}} , we define a notion of weak 𝒪 {\mathcal{O}} -monoids — which we term 𝒪 {\mathcal{O}} -pseudomonoids – in a 2-category. In the special case with the 2-category in question is the 2-category 𝖢𝖺𝗍 {\mathsf{Cat}} of categories, this yields a notion of 𝒪 {\mathcal{O}} -monoidal category, which in the case of the associative and commutative operads retrieves unbiased notions of monoidal and symmetric monoidal categories, respectively.

arxiv-2404-02687.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation with Karma: An Experimental Study
arxiv-2404-02687.creator: Ezzat Elokda, Saverio Bolognani, Florian Dörfler, Heinrich H. Nax
arxiv-2404-02687.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ezzat Elokda, Saverio Bolognani, Florian Dörfler, Heinrich H. Nax. We perform a behavioral experiment of karma , a class of mechanisms for repeated resource allocation with attractive fairness and efficiency properties, in theory. Individuals in these mechanisms bid non-tradable credits that flow from resource consumers to yielders. Human subjects recruited on Amazon MTurk are repeatedly and randomly paired to bid karma according to time-varying individual urgency to acquire resources.

arxiv-2405-20039.title: Task-Agnostic Machine-Learning-Assisted Inference
arxiv-2405-20039.creator: Jiacheng Miao, Qiongshi Lu
arxiv-2405-20039.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) is playing an increasingly important role in scientific research. In conjunction with classical statistical approaches, ML-assisted analytical strategies have shown great promise in accelerating research findings. This has also opened a whole field of methodological research focusing on integrative approaches that leverage both ML and statistics to tackle data science challenges.

arxiv-2408-04528.title: Reasoning about Study Regulations in Answer Set Programming Thanks: A preliminary version of this article appeared in ( Hahn et al., 2023 ) .
arxiv-2408-04528.creator: SUSANA HAHN, CEDRIC MARTENS, AMADE NEMES, HENRY OTUNUYA, JAVIER ROMERO, TORSTEN SCHAUB, SEBASTIAN SCHELLHORN
arxiv-2408-04528.description: Abstract We are interested in automating reasoning with and about study regulations, catering to various stakeholders, ranging from administrators, over faculty, to students at different stages. Our work builds on an extensive analysis of various study programs at the University of Potsdam. The conceptualization of the underlying principles provides us with a formal account of study regulations.

arxiv-2505-08713.title: Self-scalings of bubble pinch-off and inner jet emitting in a tapered co-flow
arxiv-2505-08713.creator: B. J. Ruan, Z. L. Wang
arxiv-2505-08713.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by B. J. Ruan, Z. L. Wang. This study systematically investigates the formation mechanisms and scaling laws governing sub-millimeter bubble-jet generation in convergent coaxial microchannels. Experimental observations reveal four distinct evolutionary stages in monodisperse bubble formation: growth, necking, detachment, and stabilization. Through necking rupture dynamics modeling, we demonstrate that the coupled effects of nozzle insertion length ( x x ) and convergence angle ( α \alpha ) dominate neck width evolution, exhibiting universal power-law scaling across geometric configurations.

arxiv-2510-22265.title: Error bounded compression for weather and climate applications
arxiv-2510-22265.description: Abstract As the resolution of weather and climate simulations increases, the amount of data produced is growing rapidly from hundreds of terabytes to tens of petabytes. The huge size becomes a limiting factor for broader adoption, and its fast growth rate will soon exhaust all the available storage devices. To address these issues, we present EBCC (Error Bounded Climate-data Compressor).

arxiv-2511-21791.title: Ealy’s conjecture in odd characteristic
arxiv-2511-21791.creator: Tao Feng, Koen Thas
arxiv-2511-21791.description: Abstract . We solve Ealy’s conjecture from 1977 by showing that for each odd prime p p , a finite generalized quadrangle each point of which admits a central symmetry of order p p , is either a classical symplectic quadrangle in dimension 3 3 , or a Hermitian quadrangle in dimension 3 3 or 4 4 .

europmc-pmc8745566.creator: Niland S, Riscanevo AX, Eble JA.
europmc-pmc8745566.description: Cancer progression with uncontrolled tumor growth, local invasion, and metastasis depends largely on the proteolytic activity of numerous matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), which affect tissue integrity, immune cell recruitment, and tissue turnover by degrading extracellular...

pmc-11436872.title: Unleashing the power of AI in science-key considerations for materials data preparation
pmc-11436872.creator: Yongchao Lu, Hong Wang, Lanting Zhang, Ning Yu, Siqi Shi, Hang Su
pmc-11436872.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The release of ChatGPT has triggered global attention on artificial intelligence (AI), and AI for science is thus becoming a hot topic in the scientific community. When we think about unleashing the power of AI to accelerate scientific research, the question coming to our mind first is whether there is a continuous supply of highly available data at a sufficiently large scale.

pmc-11494560.title: Sivelestat protects against acute lung injury by up-regulating angiotensin-converting enzyme 2/angiotensin-(1–7)/Mas receptors
pmc-11494560.creator: Changqing He, Ruoxin Li, Jia Zhang, Wenshu Chai
pmc-11494560.description: BackgroundAcute lung injury (ALI) and its most severe manifestation of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a disease with a clinical mortality rate of up to 40% and is one of the most dangerous and common complications of severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Sivelestat (SIV) is the only licensed therapeutic medicine in the world for ALI/ARDS treatment.

pmc-11600619.title: Effects of propofol on the electrophysiological properties of glutamatergic neurons in the ventrolateral medulla of mice
pmc-11600619.creator: Ya Chen, Tian Yu, Junli Jiang
pmc-11600619.description: BackgroundPropofol, a commonly used intravenous anesthetic, is associated with various respiratory adverse events, most notably different degrees of respiratory depression, which pose significant concerns for patient safety. Respiration is a fundamental behavior, with the initiation of breathing in mammals dependent on neuronal activity in the lower brainstem.

pmc-11612164.title: Deciphering the pharmacological mechanism of Radix astragali for allergic rhinitis through network pharmacology and experimental validation
pmc-11612164.creator: Yiwei Hua, Xi Tan, Jingwen Zhang, Ningcong Xu, Ruien Chen, Shiqing Zhou, Shaoqing Liu, Kai Li, Wenyong Chen, Qiulan Luo, Yunying Li
pmc-11612164.description: Radix Astragali (RA) has been recognized for its therapeutic potential in allergic rhinitis (AR), yet its potential pharmacological mechanisms remain elusive. This study systematically investigated the physicochemical properties and biological activities of RA’s phytochemicals, aiming to elucidate their targets and mechanisms in AR treatment.

pmc-11702980.title: Generating fragrant oilseed rape using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing
pmc-11702980.creator: Jian Wu, Jingyi Xu, Ancheng He, Sichao Ren, Yi Ye, Wenjing Lei, Yu Liu, Xia Hua, Chunjie Wei, Li Lin, Hui Zhang, Youping Wang
pmc-11702980.description: Knocking out 2 functionally redundant aldehyde dehydrogenase-encoding genes via gene editing leads to 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline accumulation in oilseed rape, which can be used to develop fragrant lines. Dear Editor, Oilseed rape (OSR, Brassica napus L.) is the third-largest oilseed crop worldwide and the largest in China. OSR is also an exceptional source of early green fodder, haylage, and high-protein cake/meal.

pmc-12543186.title: Discovery of C-12 dithiocarbamate andrographolide analogue as a novel antioxidant and α-glucosidase inhibitors: In vitro and in silico studies
pmc-12543186.creator: Utid Suriya, Chanathip Duangtha, Thanchanok Dontricharoen, Paveena Yamanont, Sakonwan Kuhaudomlarp, Prawit Thitiyanuwat, Bodee Nutho, Patcharee Arsakhant, Rungnapha Saeeng, Noppawan Phumala Morales, Supachoke Mangmool, Sutharinee Likitnukul
pmc-12543186.description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a global health issue associated with oxidative stress, inflammation, and insulin resistance. Even though α-glucosidase inhibitors such as acarbose are used in treatment, their efficacy is limited by gastrointestinal side effects. In this study, we evaluated the antioxidant properties and α-glucosidase inhibition of C-12 dithiocarbamate andrographolide analogues compared to the parent compound, andrographolide.

pmc-13126274.title: JAK2 V617F mutations and thrombosis in BCR-ABL1 negative myeloproliferative neoplasms: clinical profile and hematologic insights
pmc-13126274.creator: Anna Mira Lubis, Muhammad Orri Baskoro, Gabriella Anindyah, Agnes Stephanie Harahap
pmc-13126274.description: BackgroundThe interplay between JAK2 mutation, thrombosis, and the baseline clinical and hematologic profile of MPN remains poorly understood. This study aims to provide insight on the relationship between the clinical profile and hematologic findings, JAK2 V617F mutation, and the occurrence of thrombotic events in BCR-ABL1 negative MPNs.

pmc-13618591.title: Public Engagement to Inform Messaging Aligning With the Muscle‐Strengthening Guidelines
pmc-13618591.creator: Ashley Gluchowski
pmc-13618591.description: IntroductionPhysical activity guidelines and their supplementary messaging play a fundamental role in raising awareness and increasing knowledge at a population level. In the United Kingdom, there are no national‐level messaging campaigns accompanying the strength component of their physical activity guidelines for public health.

pmc-13682945.title: In vitro incubation of human sperm does not change DNA methylation
pmc-13682945.creator: Emma Tykesson Kjøller, Marie-Charlotte Dumargne, Lars Roed Ingerslev, Eleonora Manitta, Yasmin Dehestani, Marte Saupstad, Alba Gonzalez-Franquesa, Atul Shahaji Deshmukh, Emil Andersen, Romain Barrès
pmc-13682945.description: STUDY QUESTIONIs DNA methylation in mature spermatozoa affected by different culture media?SUMMARY ANSWERIncubation of mature spermatozoa in hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) or palmitate for 24 h did not alter the DNA methylome.WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADYChildren conceived through ART face a higher risk of disorders linked to abnormal DNA methylation.
